reason: Section 125 is a very large regulation-making source whose topics divide into regulation subjects, application/effect rules, zoning regulation powers, subdivision regulation powers, public-purpose land and money, and consultation or filing rules.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Planning and development regulation-making subjects

evidenceText: may make regulations

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 125(1) lists the matters on which the Lieutenant-Governor in Council may make regulations, including setbacks, mobile home parks, service stations, signs, excavation, subdivision, lots, wastewater, pool fences, building work, approvals, wiring permits, land use policies, and council-equivalent powers.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the planning and development subjects that may be governed by regulations under section 125.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Fees, area designation, local effectiveness, priority, and rural-plan consistency for regulations

evidenceText: the regulation under paragraph (1)(j) prevails

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections cover fee payment to regional service commissions, area designation, municipal or rural community effectiveness, paragraph 125(1)(j) effectiveness and priority, and rural-plan consistency.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how section 125 regulations are paid for, where they apply, when they are effective locally, when land-use policy regulations prevail, and when consistency with rural plans is required.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Development officer status and zoning regulation powers

evidenceText: the planning director as defined in the Regional Services Delivery Act is the development officer

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections make the planning director the development officer when a regulation is in effect and set special powers for zoning regulations or zoning provisions, including regional service commission powers, temporary authorization letters, fees, variances, and Minister rezoning orders or agreements.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who acts as development officer under section 125 regulations and what special zoning-related powers may be vested or deemed vested.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Subdivision regulation public-purpose land, access, approval, fees, street names, exemptions, variances, and subdivision provisions

evidenceText: A subdivision regulation under this section may

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections authorize subdivision regulation rules for public-purpose land and money, regional service commission access and approval powers, tentative-plan fees, street names, exemptions, section 77 application, Minister approval for public-purpose land, variances, and sections 79 and 80.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the subdivision regulation powers and how subdivision by-law provisions apply when a subdivision regulation is in effect.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Crown land for public purposes and Minister special accounts

evidenceText: Land vested in the Crown under this section

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections govern land vested in the Crown for public purposes and how money received in lieu of land or from sale must be held, invested, spent, and transferred if the subdivision later enters a local government.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how Crown public-purpose land and money in lieu of land are held, spent, invested, and transferred under section 125.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Pre-making views and notice, rural plan summaries, and land registration filing for regulations

evidenceText: Before making a regulation under this section

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections require regional service commission or advisory committee views and section 111-like procedure before regulations, allow written summaries for some zoning regulations or rural plans, and require filing copies in affected county land registration offices.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the consultation, notice, summary, and land registration filing rules before or after making section 125 regulations.

reason: Section 126 is a focused administration and non-delegation rule for the Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minister administration and non-delegable powers

evidenceText: shall not delegate the powers

proposedGroups.reason: The subsections make the Minister responsible for administration, allow designations to act on the Minister's behalf, and prohibit delegation of powers under sections 51, 125, and 132.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who administers the Act and which Ministerial powers cannot be delegated.

reason: Section 126.1 states a single comprehensive review duty with a review deadline and report deadline.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Comprehensive review of the Act and report to the Legislative Assembly

evidenceText: shall undertake a comprehensive review

proposedGroups.reason: The section requires the Minister to review the operation of the Act within seven years after January 1, 2023, and report within one year or further time allowed.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when the Minister must review the Act and submit the review report.

reason: Section 127 is a coherent fee by-law rule for specified community planning and development services.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Fee by-laws for planning and development services and regional service commission collections

evidenceText: may make a by-law prescribing fees

proposedGroups.reason: The subsections list services for which council may prescribe fees and state that fees collected by a regional service commission are paid to the local government in the region.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what planning and development service fees council may prescribe and where regional service commission-collected fees are paid.

reason: Section 128 is a focused approval authority for pipeline construction.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Development officer approvals for pipeline construction

evidenceText: may grant approvals for pipeline construction

proposedGroups.reason: The section authorizes a development officer to grant pipeline construction approvals when the development officer is the approving authority under the Pipeline Act, 2005.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when a development officer may grant approvals for pipeline construction.

reason: Section 129 is a substantive compliance rule for development on Crown-owned land by non-Crown persons.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: No exemption from planning compliance for development on Crown land

evidenceText: is not exempt from compliance

proposedGroups.reason: The section states that a person, except the Crown or its agent, is not exempt from complying with the Act, by-laws, regulations, orders, demands, terms, conditions, or Board decisions merely because the land is Crown-owned.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that Crown ownership of land does not exempt non-Crown persons from planning compliance.

reason: Section 130 is a coherent evidence rule for certified copies of by-laws, resolutions, and clerk-filed records.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Certified by-law, resolution, and clerk record copies as court evidence

evidenceText: is evidence in all courts

proposedGroups.reason: The subsections make certified copies evidence of passage, existence, adoption or making dates, and filed or deposited records without proof of the clerk's official character or handwriting.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how certified copies of council by-laws, resolutions, and clerk-filed records serve as court evidence.

reason: Section 131 separates developer agreement triggers and parties from filing/binding effects and breach or discharge powers.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Council or Minister agreements with developers for additional or imposed conditions

evidenceText: may enter into an agreement with the developer

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 131(1) identifies when additional or imposed development conditions may be secured by agreement and whether council or the Minister may enter it.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when council or the Minister may enter an agreement with a developer to ensure performance of development conditions.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Developer agreement filing, binding effect, breach work, discharge, and discharge filing

evidenceText: on breach of the agreement and after giving 30 days

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections apply filing and binding rules, allow entry and performance after breach and 30 days' notice, allow discharge of covenants or conditions, and require discharge filing within ten days of filing the agreement.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how developer agreements are filed and enforced, and how covenants or conditions may be discharged and filed.

reason: Section 132 separates Ministerial approval, quashing, order, and takeover powers from advisory committee appointment and revesting of powers.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Lieutenant-Governor approval, quashing by-laws, ordering conformity, and Minister takeover of council powers

evidenceText: shall not exercise a power under this section except with the approval

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections require Lieutenant-Governor in Council approval for section 132 powers, allow the Minister to quash by-laws, order local government conformity or enforcement, and exercise council powers after non-compliance with an order.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the Minister's approved powers to quash by-laws, order conformity or enforcement, and take over council powers.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minister-appointed advisory committee and revesting powers in council

evidenceText: may appoint

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections allow appointment of five advisory committee members when the Minister exercises council powers for a local government with its own planning service and allow the Minister to revest powers in council by notice and filing.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how advisory committee appointments and revesting of powers work when the Minister has taken over council powers.

reason: Section 133 is a coherent inspection workflow for suspected planning violations and resulting orders.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Inspection of property, entry warrants, dwelling limits, and written orders

evidenceText: may, at all reasonable times

proposedGroups.reason: The subsections authorize entry with consent on reasonable grounds, allow entry warrant applications, restrict entry to private dwellings, and permit service of a written order after a violation is found.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who may inspect for suspected planning violations, when warrants or dwelling consent are needed, and when an order may be served.

reason: Section 134 is a substantial violation-order source with distinct topics for order powers, service and deadlines, and compliance or cost recovery.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Violation orders to stop, alter, or restore development

evidenceText: may order

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 134(1) identifies who may order cessation, alteration to remove a violation, or restoration after development violates the Act, by-laws, regulations, or imposed terms and conditions.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who may issue violation orders and what cessation, alteration, or restoration actions may be ordered.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Written order contents, service, deadlines, cessation service, and deemed mail service

evidenceText: be in writing and signed

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections require signed written orders, service on owners, grounds and compliance periods, additional service for cessation orders, and deemed service four days after mailing.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how violation orders must be written, served, timed, and deemed served by registered mail.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Owner compliance, action by Director or council, cost recovery, and lien

evidenceText: shall comply with the order at their own expense

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections require owner compliance at the owner's expense, allow the Director or council to undertake the ordered action and sue for costs, and make those costs a lien until recovered.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the owner's compliance duty and how costs of unmet violation orders may be recovered and secured by lien.

reason: Section 135 is a coherent court-enforcement application and order provision for violations, failures, and obstruction.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Court orders for violations, failures, obstruction, removal, destruction, and costs

evidenceText: may make an application to The Court

proposedGroups.reason: The subsections identify who may apply to the Court for enforcement orders and list possible restraining, removal, destruction, enforcement, cost, and expense-recovery orders.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when local government, the Minister, or a designated person may seek court orders and what orders the judge may make.
